founding_year.basis: 'In 1999, three partners from IVP joined with three partners from Brentwood Venture Capital to form two new firms: Redpoint Ventures...' Corroborated by the fund ladder (Redpoint Ventures I LP, CIK 1098978, on EDGAR from 1999) and by the firm's own 2007 announcement archive.

history.value: Redpoint Ventures was founded in 1999 in Menlo Park by six partners who left two firms at once: Brad Jones, Jeff Brody and Tim Haley from Brentwood Venture Capital, and Geoff Yang, Tom Dyal and John Walecka from Institutional Venture Partners. The two firms' information-technology practices combined into Redpoint while their healthcare and life-science practices went the other way into Versant Ventures, and the partners' pre-1999 deals stayed behind: the firm's own early site carried them in a separate table headed 'Previous Investments by Redpoint Partners'. Redpoint raised a $600M first fund in 1999 and a $1.25B second fund in 2000, invested through the telecom and optical bust, and rebuilt around consumer internet and infrastructure. It added a growth sleeve, Redpoint Omega, in 2007, a China effort in 2005 that became a separate firm in 2015, and a Brazilian joint venture with e.ventures in 2012. The firm moved from 3000 Sand Hill Road to Woodside in 2022 and today runs two fund lines side by side, the early-stage Redpoint Ventures series (X, $650M, 2025) and the growth-stage Redpoint Omega series (V, $740M, 2024).
history.basis: The spin-out is documented in the partners' own bios on the firm's 2000-2006 site ('Prior to founding Redpoint, Geoff was a general partner with IVP'), in the Versant Ventures and IVP articles the Wikipedia insource sweep returned, and in the firm's own two-section portfolio table. Fund sizes from the Form D ladder and the firm's own announcement archive.

investment_concept.value: Two vehicles, one partnership: an early-stage fund that leads seed and Series A rounds and a growth fund that enters at Series B and later, with the same partners working both. The firm publishes a one-line entry claim on every company page (“We first partnered for their Series C in 2012”), which makes its own stage discipline unusually legible: 58% of the companies recorded here entered at Series A, 13% at seed and 28% at growth.
investment_concept.basis: The two fund lines are the firm's own EDGAR structure (Redpoint Ventures I-X early, Redpoint Omega I-V growth, both under CRD 161680); the stage shares are computed off this run's landed entry_stage column (240 Series A, 118 Growth, 56 Seed, 3 Pre-Seed on 417 rows).

investment_stage.basis: DERIVED, not taken from a site filter: the firm publishes no stage vocabulary of its own beyond the four-value taxonomy on its company cards. The landed distribution is Series A 58%, Growth 28%, Seed 13%, Pre-Seed 1%, and the fund architecture (an early series and a growth series) matches it.

investment_geo.basis: Landed hq_country distribution over the 412-row base: US 353 (86%), China 29 (7%), Israel 11, UK 5, Canada 4, Brazil 4, and eight countries with one or two rows. The core is one label, inside the two-label cap. China is expressed as **Asia**, the label data/taxonomy/geo.json carries — the ingest rejected 'China' as an unknown geography and would have added it to the taxonomy, which COLLECTION.md 11 forbids (an investor-specific vocabulary is never unioned into a closed list). It sits in `other` rather than `core` because the whole of it predates the 2015 spin-out of Redpoint China (decisions.md D2) and the firm has listed no new Chinese company since.

investment_range.basis: MEDIAN: the Form D entry-round distribution over the 85 base rows whose first filed round is on EDGAR — median $6.93M, p25 $3.0M, p75 $18.0M — published as $7M. It is a ROUND-SIZE PROXY for check size and is fair here only because Redpoint leads most of its early rounds; it also skews low because Form D coverage starts in 2009 and misses the paper era and the 4(a)(2) seeds. LOWER LIMIT: $2M, the scale of the smallest first rounds in that distribution and of the firm's own smallest seed announcements. UPPER LIMIT: $100M, from a 10-15% single-position concentration of the largest fund (Redpoint Omega V, $740M sworn), cross-checked against the largest rounds the firm says it led (Flora $42M Series A, JetStream $34M seed) and its participations in $250M+ growth rounds. Strategy allocations and aggregator 'typical check' claims were rejected.

notable_investments.basis: Recognition over the confirmed base only: every name is a ledger-verified member of this run's 417-row base. NETFLIX WAS REMOVED after the grind ruled it not_member under decisions.md D5 — the firm's own 2000-2006 site lists it under 'Previous Investments by Redpoint Partners' and the live card dates the relationship to 1998, a year before the firm existed. ARISTA NETWORKS WAS ALSO REMOVED, on Erik's T3 ruling of 2026-09-06 (no round named + partnered after IPO), which took it out of the base along with Juniper Networks, Concur and Internet Brands.

aum.basis: Redpoint Management, LLC is an EXEMPT REPORTING ADVISER (SEC 802-75525, CRD 161680), so no Item 5.F regulatory AUM exists. The sworn substitute is Schedule D Section 7.B.(1): 35 private funds whose current gross asset values sum to $7,964,567,728 on the annual amendment filed 2026-04-01 (parsed to sources/registers/adv-7b-funds.json). Both range ends are that number because no credible press figure sits above it. ONE FINDING WORTH RECORDING: Redpoint names NONE of its funds in the ADV — every Section 7.B entry uses a colour or fruit code (FUND MAGENTA, BLUSH SIDE FUND) under the rule 204-2(d) anonymity option the form itself offers, so the sworn roster anchors the AUM but cannot be mapped onto the named funds. The fund table is built from the vehicles' own Form D filings instead.

funds.basis: Seventeen entries: the two fund lines plus the two paper-era side vehicles. Every 2010-and-later entry carries its own Form D accession and the filed total-offering amount, asserted at build time. The 1999-2007 vintages predate mandatory electronic Form D, so Ventures I ($600M) and II ($1.25B) take the firm's own announcement-archive figures and Ventures III, Technology Partners A-1/Q-1 and Omega I carry null sizes with the reason. The lettered Omega co-invest vehicles (III-MC, IV-C, IV-F, IV-G, IV-I, IV-L, IV-R, IV-Y) and the Entrepreneurs Funds IV and V are counted and described here rather than listed: eleven single-deal or employee vehicles filing $3.5M-$51M offerings, all under the same adviser (decisions.md D1). The 2016 $180M China fund and the 2012 $130M Redpoint e.ventures Brazil fund are DELIBERATELY ABSENT — both sit outside the boundary under decisions.md D2 and D4. Four entries (Omega III, Ventures VIII, Omega IV, Ventures IX) carry the total-offering amount WITHOUT an accession assertion because their Form Ds were filed at $0 sold before first close — the Accel-style cross-check does not apply to them and COLLECTION.md 11's rule is followed explicitly.
